findings.title: Dismissing the backup-codes dialog with Esc/overlay leaves the UI saying 2FA is off
findings.body: `onEnable()` is no longer called when the TOTP code is verified. It now runs only from the "Close" button on the new DisplayBackupCodes step. By then 2FA is already enabled server-side. If the user dismisses the dialog with Escape or by clicking outside, only `onOpenChange` fires. As far as I can tell the parent's `onEnable` is what marks 2FA as enabled, and `onOpenChange` just toggles the modal. The settings switch then shows 2FA as disabled while it is active. `step` is never reset either, so reopening the modal lands back on the backup-codes screen. The step needs to be reset and `onEnable` called whenever the dialog closes from that step, not only from the Close button.

findings.title: "missing_backup_codes" tells users to generate codes in settings, but no such feature exists
findings.body: The message says "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." Codes are only generated inside the 2FA setup endpoint, and there is no UI or API to regenerate them. Every user who enabled 2FA before this migration has `backupCodes = null`. Choosing "Lost access" shows them this message with nothing they can do. To disable 2FA and re-enable it they would need their TOTP code, which is what they lost. Either add a regenerate flow or change the message so it does not point to a nonexistent setting.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so a code can be used twice
findings.body: The user row is read at the top of `authorize`. The code is nulled in memory and the whole encrypted blob is written back with an unconditional `update`. Two concurrent logins with the same backup code both read the unconsumed list, both pass `indexOf`, and both succeed. This breaks the "each code can be used exactly once" guarantee. The write can also overwrite a concurrent update to `backupCodes`. Use a transaction with a row lock, or an optimistic check that the stored value is unchanged (compare-and-swap).

findings.title: Backup code comparison is case- and whitespace-sensitive, while the UI placeholder suggests uppercase
findings.body: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`). The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which suggests uppercase. The comparison only strips `-` and does not lowercase or trim. A user who types or pastes the code in uppercase, or with stray whitespace, gets "Backup code is incorrect". This is a usability problem at exactly the moment the user is locked out. The same logic is duplicated in the disable endpoint.

findings.title: Submitting an empty backup code silently does nothing
findings.body: The login form has `noValidate`, so the `required`, `minLength` and `maxLength` attributes on the BackupCode input are not enforced. If the user submits with the field empty, `credentials.backupCode` is falsy and the server falls into the TOTP branch. It throws `SecondFactorRequired`. The client handles that by calling `setTwoFactorRequired(true)`, which is already true, and shows no error. The user sees no feedback. Show an error message, or validate the field in the zod schema when in lost-access mode.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode in the request body causes an unhandled TypeError (500)
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode` is only checked for truthiness. If a client sends a non-string truthy value such as an object, number or array, `.replaceAll` is not a function and the handler throws an unhandled exception that becomes a 500. The input should be validated as a string (for example with zod) and rejected with a 400/`IncorrectBackupCode`.

findings.title: tabIndex={-1} added to the shared PasswordField toggle button
findings.body: This changes the shared `PasswordField` component, so every password input in the app is affected. Keyboard-only and screen-reader users can no longer tab to the show/hide password toggle. It was probably added to make tabbing through the login form smoother, but it removes an accessible control everywhere. It is unrelated to backup codes and should be scoped to the login page, or reverted.

findings.title: Core backup-code flows (login and disable with a backup code) have no tests
findings.body: The new e2e coverage only checks that the download and copy buttons exist and that the dialog closes. Nothing tests logging in with a backup code, a code being invalidated after use, wrong-code errors, or disabling 2FA with a backup code. Those are the security-sensitive paths this PR adds, and the TODO acknowledges the gap. The download and clipboard contents are not checked either. The first test's `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise and always passes, so it does not verify 2FA is enabled (the FIXME notes this). The PR checklist also admits no tests were added.

findings.title: Copy button shows success toast without awaiting the clipboard write; codes and blob URL linger after close
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught. The "Backup codes copied!" toast shows even if the write is rejected (permission denied, insecure context). The user may believe the codes are saved when they are not. Separately, `resetState()` does not clear `backupCodes`, `secret`, `dataUri`, or `backupCodesUrl`. The Blob object URL containing all plaintext codes is never revoked on close or unmount, so the secrets stay in memory until the next setup.
